event_text: Vietnam War: The House Un-American Activities Committee begins investigations of Americans who have aided the Viet Cong. The committee intends to introduce legislation making these activities illegal. Anti-war demonstrators disrupt the meeting and 50 people are arrested.
headline: HUAC Launches Probe into Viet Cong Sympathizers
story: Barry pecked at a stray crumb on the windowsill. 'Ah, 1966, and the House Un-American Activities Committee is at it again, Susan. This time, they're after Americans who've been helping the Viet Cong. Chairman Edwin Willis is leading the charge, determined to root out those un-American activities.' Susan preened her feathers. 'Fifty people arrested today, I see. All very dramatic. The committee's planning to introduce legislation to make aiding the Viet Cong a crime. One wonders what constitutes "aiding" – a care package, perhaps, or a strongly worded letter to the editor?' Barry snorted. 'I'm sure it'll all be very carefully defined. After all, one can't have Americans questioning the war effort. That would be, well, un-American.' Susan gazed out the window, where anti-war demonstrators were being led away in handcuffs. 'It's all so very...1960s. The Red Scare all over again, with a dash of Vietnam-era paranoia.'
regret_line: It seems hindsight is 20/20, especially when it comes to McCarthy-esque witch hunts.
winner_line: The militarized concept of patriotism, which managed to silence dissent and fuel the war machine for years to come.
